66.title: [P1] Do not execute mutable issue content as trusted AFK instructions
66.body:
<!-- ralph-milestone-finding pr:61 id:422a13f32d983df171ec -->
## Context

**Source:** automated milestone review of PR #61
**Milestone:** Phase 1: Core Profile API (Tracer Bullet)
**Reviewed head:** `aa63f8a3c103ac93e75c485e2b84e4918cf944ac`
**Severity:** P1
**Location:** `scripts/ralph/ralph-loop.mjs:975`

## Finding

Issue bodies are copied verbatim into a workspace-write Codex prompt without validating author association or an approved content hash. An external issue author can edit the body after milestone assignment; generated changes are subsequently validated outside the sandbox, committed, and pushed by a credentialed process. Restrict inputs to trusted authors or immutable approved snapshots, sanitize the child environment, and execute generated validation scripts in a credential-free isolation boundary.

## Definition of done

- Fix the root cause without weakening existing behavior or tests.
- Add or update regression coverage for the failure path.
- Run the relevant checks from AGENTS.md and the Ralph configuration.
- Keep the change focused on this finding; do not create a pull request.

The existing draft PR will be updated and reviewed again after all review findings are resolved.

<!-- ralph-issue-review-context:start -->
## Ralph Loop: independent review found problems

The cached-image return is fixed at HEAD, but the AFK trust and validation boundaries still have actionable gaps; the focused Ralph suite could not complete here because temp-directory writes are sandbox-blocked.

- **P1 — Keep the approved-snapshot ledger outside the agent-writable workspace** (scripts/ralph/ralph-loop.mjs:484)
  The default approval ledger is `scripts/ralph/approved-issues.json`, while Codex is launched with `workspace-write`. An AFK session can therefore modify the ledger, have that modification committed and pushed, and a later Ralph invocation will load the modified snapshot as trusted input. This makes the purported immutable approval source mutable by the process it is meant to constrain. Store it in the protected read-only instruction area (or otherwise enforce its integrity before every run) and add a regression test for attempted ledger modification.
- **P1 — Do not run generated npm lifecycle hooks in the unrestricted Docker build stage** (scripts/ralph/Dockerfile.validation:14)
  The validation image is built from the post-agent workspace, and `RUN npm ci` executes lifecycle hooks from its generated `package.json`/lockfile. That build step has Docker's default root user and network access; only the later migration layer and `docker run` are network-disabled. A generated `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall` thus executes outside the promised network-disabled validation boundary. Build dependencies from trusted inputs, or disable lifecycle hooks and explicitly provision required runtime assets within the constrained boundary; cover the failure path with a behavioral test.
- **P2 — Update the primary Ralph operator guide for isolated validation** (.agents/RALPH.md:21)
  The primary guide still says `db:ready` starts host PostgreSQL and that full checks run outside the sandbox. Current Ralph code instead runs preflight and validation in fresh network-disabled containers with ephemeral PostgreSQL. This misstates both the required host setup and the security boundary; update `.agents/RALPH.md` to match the containerized workflow.
<!-- ralph-issue-review-context:end -->
